newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy in secret visit amid Bahamas fallout.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy in secret visit amid Bahamas fallout.

text.p: Foreign Minister John Chang has quietly left Taiwan on a secretive trip abroad, just after the diplomatically isolated island severed ties with the Bahamas, Chang's office said on Tuesday.
"Minister Chang is out of the country. We will give more details of his visit in a few days," Chang's office told Reuters by telephone.
Following a pattern set in earlier clandestine overseas missions by senior Taiwan officials, the ministry declined even to confirm media reports that Chang was on his way to Europe.
As Taiwan has but one diplomatic ally in Europe, the Vatican, a visit by Chang anywhere else on the continent is sure to trigger protests from arch rival communist China.

Beijing, which has viewed the island as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949, has steadily tightened a diplomatic squeeze on Taipei in a quest to bring Taiwan under mainland rule, warning other countries not to exchange ties with Taipei or permit visits by senior Taiwan officials.

Chang's departure late on Monday came just one day after Taiwan brusquely severed ties with the Bahamas, withdrew its ambassador and ended all treaties and aid after learning the Caribbean nation was preparing to secure ties with Beijing.

It was the first time Taipei had taken such pre-emptive action in its diplomatic tug-of-war with Beijing, reflecting a new strategy of trying to make such switches economically painful so allies will think twice before acting.
Taipei hoped to avert the "domino effect", a nightmare scenario in which one defection triggered a series, Chang said.

The China Times said Chang would likely visit Brussels first and then other European countries during a tour lasting more than 10 days. The United Daily News said Chang might visit unidentified nations in Africa, home of several Taiwan allies.
Local media speculated that an African tour might be linked to Taiwan's new but already troubled ties with the tiny West African state of Sao Tome and Principe.
Chang on Saturday said Taiwan would not give up its formal ties with Sao Tome, established on May 6, despite reports that Sao Tome's cabinet had rejected the new links.
Beijing voiced strong opposition to Sao Tome establishing diplomatic relations with Taiwan but stopped short of saying it would sever official ties with the debt-mired African republic.
Now that ties with the Bahamas have been severed, Taiwan has diplomatic links with only 30 states, most of them small, poor and heavily dependent on Taipei's financial largesse.
The number soon will fall to 29, as top ally South Africa has said it would switch ties in 1997.
To evade China's diplomatic embargo, Taiwan has engaged in what it calls "pragmatic diplomacy" -- quiet, unofficial visits to countries which recognise Beijing instead of Taipei.
Between them, Premier Lien Chan and Chang have made such visits to Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, Belgium, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the past year.
